query_text: tips to avoid fake job scams

messages.content: tips to avoid fake job scams

message.content:
Common ways to avoid **fake job scams** are to verify the company, never pay money upfront, and be cautious of offers that seem too good to be true.[3][4][6]

- **Research the employer**: search the company name plus “scam,” “review,” or “complaint,” and check whether it has a real website, contact details, and a professional online presence.[1][3][4]
- **Verify the recruiter**: look up the recruiter’s name, company, email domain, and phone number to confirm they match the business’s official details.[1][5]
- **Watch for “too good to be true” offers**: unusually high pay for little work, no experience required, or guaranteed fast money are classic warning signs.[2][3][6]
- **Be cautious if there is no real interview**: offers made without an interview, or with only a very short or unusual interview, are suspicious.[2][5][6]
- **Never pay to get hired**: legitimate employers do not ask for application fees, training fees, equipment fees, or other upfront payments.[3][4][6]
- **Do not send money back from a check**: fake-check scams often involve depositing a check and sending part of it elsewhere; honest employers do not do this.[3][4]
- **Do not share sensitive personal information early**: be wary if someone asks for your Social Security number, bank details, credit card number, or driver’s license before you are hired.[5][6]
- **Be suspicious of urgency**: scammers often pressure you to act immediately so you do not have time to verify the job.[6]
- **Ask someone you trust**: talking through the offer with a friend, family member, or career advisor can help you spot red flags.[3][4]

If you want, I can also give you a **quick checklist** for spotting job scams in emails, texts, and LinkedIn messages.
